hints: Focus on the one structural feature that allows addition polymerisation, a carbon-carbon double bond that can open up to join monomers.
Check formulae 1 and 2 first, as both $	ext{C}_4	ext{H}_8$ (butene) and $	ext{C}_2	ext{H}_3	ext{Cl}$ (chloroethene) can easily exist as alkenes.
For $	ext{C}_3	ext{H}_6	ext{O}$, remember the same atoms can be arranged in different ways, so look for an isomer that still contains C=C alongside the O.
walkthrough:
**Recall the monomer requirement**

Think simple and visual. Addition polymerisation only happens when a small alkene monomer has a C=C double bond to open and link.

Rule to use:
$$\text{monomer must contain C=C} \rightarrow \text{addition polymer}$$

**Test formula 1: $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$**

This is the general formula for an alkene, $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$. It can be but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, or methylpropene.

Conclusion: 1 is correct, it polymerises to poly(butene).

**Test formula 2: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$**

Replace one H of ethene with Cl and you get chloroethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$. This still has the vital C=C bond.

Conclusion: 2 is correct, it polymerises to PVC, poly(chloroethene).

**Test the tricky one: $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$**

Many students stop at propanal or propanone, which cannot do addition polymerisation. But the question asks for at least one compound.

Consider the unsaturated alcohol isomer:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$$ 
This is prop-2-en-1-ol. It contains both OH and C=C, so the C=C part can undergo addition polymerisation.

Conclusion: 3 is also correct, so 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. All three formulae can represent an alkene monomer. 1 is butene, 2 is chloroethene, and 3 can be an unsaturated alcohol or ether such as CH2=CH-CH2-OH which still has C=C for addition polymerisation.
options.B: Incorrect. This option suggests only 1 and 2 work. Students choose this when they think C3H6O must be a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) and forget about functional group and positional isomerism with C=C.
options.C: Incorrect. This option leaves out 1. C4H8 is a classic alkene formula (CnH2n) and clearly forms addition polymers like poly(butene), so it cannot be excluded.
options.D: Incorrect. This option leaves out 2 and 3. C2H3Cl is the famous PVC monomer (vinyl chloride), so excluding it is a sign of confusing addition with condensation polymerisation.
